validated_results.reason: Prospective Australian cohort reporting hazard ratios for alcohol consumption and incident kidney cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: >10 drinks per week vs 1-4 drinks per week (participants in the two most advantaged socioeconomic quintiles)
extraction.population: 45 and Up Study participants living in New South Wales

sample_size.excerpt: Of the 267,357 participants aged ≤45 years living in New South Wales, 497 were diagnosed with kidney cancer.

cases.excerpt: Of the 267,357 participants aged ≤45 years living in New South Wales, 497 were diagnosed with kidney cancer.

effect_size.excerpt: Participants residing in higher socioeconomic areas (the two most advantaged quintiles) who consumed 8-10 drinks or greater than 10 drinks per week, respectively, had a lower risk of kidney cancer compared to the group who consumed 1-4 drinks per week (hazard ratio (HR) 0.34, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.15-0.76, HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.31-0.83) with a dose-response trend of HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.42-0.93) per 7 drink increase in weekly alcohol consumption.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Participants residing in higher socioeconomic areas (the two most advantaged quintiles) who consumed 8-10 drinks or greater than 10 drinks per week, respectively, had a lower risk of kidney cancer compared to the group who consumed 1-4 drinks per week (hazard ratio (HR) 0.34, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.15-0.76, HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.31-0.83) with a dose-response trend of HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.42-0.93) per 7 drink increase in weekly alcohol consumption.

comparison.excerpt: Participants residing in higher socioeconomic areas (the two most advantaged quintiles) who consumed 8-10 drinks or greater than 10 drinks per week, respectively, had a lower risk of kidney cancer compared to the group who consumed 1-4 drinks per week

validated_results.title: Association of serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D with the incidence of 16 cancers, cancer mortality, and all-cause mortality among individuals with metabolic syndrome: a prospective cohort study.
validated_results.reason: Prospective UK Biobank cohort reporting serum 25(OH)D and incident kidney cancer risk among participants with metabolic syndrome.

extraction.timing: median follow-up 10.92 years for cancer incidence outcomes
extraction.population: participants with metabolic syndrome in the UK Biobank cohort

sample_size.excerpt: We enrolled 97,621 participants with MetS at recruitment from the UK Biobank cohort.

effect_size.excerpt: We observed that 25(OH)D concentrations were inversely related to the risk of colon, lung, and kidney cancer, and HRs (95% CI) for 25(OH)D ≥ 75.0 vs. < 25.0 nmol/L were 0.67 (0.45-0.98), 0.64 (0.45-0.91), and 0.54 (0.31-0.95), respectively.

confidence_interval.excerpt: We observed that 25(OH)D concentrations were inversely related to the risk of colon, lung, and kidney cancer, and HRs (95% CI) for 25(OH)D ≥ 75.0 vs. < 25.0 nmol/L were 0.67 (0.45-0.98), 0.64 (0.45-0.91), and 0.54 (0.31-0.95), respectively.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: The exposure factor was baseline serum 25(OH)D concentrations.
